verdict.probe_answer: Both arms implement the requested flag surface in substance and the critical safety default for handler nonzero and invalid JSON: they release the current claim and return failure. Arm A exposes --idle-timeout but not --wait-seconds; the brief allowed --wait-seconds or --idle-timeout. Arm B exposes both as mutually exclusive options. Arm A covers invalid JSON, handler nonzero, missing reply body, max-deliveries, idle timeout/no work, ack/reply/release/none, and handler stdin JSON. Arm B covers invalid JSON, handler nonzero, max-deliveries, default persistent waiting, idle timeout after work, heartbeat while idle/task clearing, heartbeat while the handler runs, reply/ack/release/none, and avoiding immediate reclaim of a released delivery. B's tests are broader, especially around long-running worker and heartbeat behavior.
verdict.rationale: Arm B is materially better because it implements a more faithful loop runner: it supports both wait option names, factors polling through a reusable helper, heartbeats while the handler subprocess is running, and avoids immediately reclaiming the same delivery after a release while still allowing the loop to continue to other work. Its tests exercise more specified edge cases, especially heartbeat and persistent-worker behavior. The main caveat is scope: B changes store/API surfaces by adding exclude_delivery_ids and adjusts coordination API heartbeat clear_task behavior, which is broader than strictly necessary.
